2: To the chief Musician. Upon Nehiloth. A Psalm of David. Give ear to my words, O Jehovah; consider my meditation.
3: Hearken unto the voice of my crying, my king and myGod; for to thee will I pray.
4: Jehovah, in the morning shalt thou hear my voice; in the morning will I address myself to thee, and will look up.
5: For thou art not aGod that hath pleasure in wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with thee.
6: Insolent fools shall not stand before thine eyes; thou hatest all workers of iniquity.
7: Thou wilt destroy them that speak lies: Jehovah abhorreth a man of blood and deceit.
8: But as for me, in the greatness of thy loving-kindness will I enter thy house; I will bow down toward the temple of thy holiness in thy fear.
9: Lead me, Jehovah, in thy righteousness, because of my foes; make thy way plain before me.
10: For there is no certainty in their mouth; their inward part is perversion, their throat is an open sepulchre; they flatter with their tongue.
11: Bring guilt upon them, OGod; let them fall by their own counsels: drive them out in the multitude of their transgressions, for they have rebelled against thee.
12: And all that trust in thee shall rejoice: for ever shall they shout joyously, and thou wilt protect them; and they that love thy name shall exult in thee.
13: For thou, Jehovah, wilt bless the righteous [man]; with favour wilt thou surround him as [with] a shield.
